summary: A screen-free conversational player that turns cards and books into adaptive audio play.
editor_note: The interface is a physical character and story card rather than another children's screen. Wippi uses voice conversation, adapts stories, remembers prior exchanges, and shifts into sleep-story modes, while a parent app exposes interactions and learning goals. That makes the hardware a boundary for AI play instead of a generic smart speaker. The open question is whether parents can independently control retention, review memory, and assess age-appropriate responses over sustained use.

product_evidence.claim: Children start conversational stories by placing physical character or story cards on the screen-free Wippi player.
The product adapts stories and remembers prior conversations, with separate sleep-story modes and a companion parent experience.

market_context.primary_user: Parents seeking interactive audio play for young children without handing them a general-purpose screen.
market_context.differentiation: Physical story objects constrain the interaction surface while conversational AI adapts audio play over time.
market_context.why_now: Voice models make open-ended audio play practical as families look for alternatives to children's screen time.

risks.claim: Parents can test whether memory controls, retention visibility, and age-appropriate response quality remain adequate over repeated use.
risks.basis: Official materials describe adaptive memory and parent visibility, but not independent child-safety or retention audits.
